body:
What is digital governance?

Digital governance, or e-governance, means using information and communication technology to deliver government information and services, process applications, maintain records and communicate with citizens. A service that once required a visit to a government office may be made available through a website, mobile application or assisted service centre.

Consider a rural resident applying for a certificate. The resident may use an internet-connected computer at a village service centre, provide the required information, undergo identity verification where necessary and receive the certificate electronically after approval. Several different technologies and government arrangements make this possible. An internet connection carries the information, an application processes the request, an authorised department approves it and a digital document system may make the certificate available.

These functions must be distinguished. Providing internet connectivity is not the same as granting a certificate, and verifying identity is not the same as deciding whether someone is eligible for a government benefit.

The Digital India programme

Digital India is an umbrella programme of the Government of India, formally launched on 1 July 2015. Its objective is to transform India into a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy. The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) coordinates the programme, while different Union ministries, state governments and implementing agencies carry out its constituent initiatives.

The programme has 3 vision areas:

  • Digital infrastructure as a core utility to every citizen: availability of connectivity, digital identity and facilities required to access digital services.
  • Governance and services on demand: electronic delivery of government services through connected and interoperable systems.
  • Digital empowerment of citizens: digital literacy and access to digital resources, including resources in Indian languages.

Distinguishing programmes, schemes and platforms

A programme may coordinate several initiatives. A scheme generally provides a defined intervention to a specified group, subject to its conditions and implementation period. A platform supplies a common technological facility used by citizens, institutions or service providers. These categories can overlap: a government programme may establish a platform, but the platform itself does not necessarily provide a cash benefit.

InitiativeMain characterPrimary purpose
Digital IndiaUmbrella programmeCoordinates digital infrastructure, services and empowerment
BharatNetConnectivity programme and infrastructureBroadband network reaching Gram Panchayats
PM-WANIPublic Wi-Fi frameworkEnables public internet access through local hotspots
PMGDISHATime-bound training schemeBasic digital literacy for eligible rural people
BHASHINILanguage technology mission and platformMultilingual digital access
AadhaarDigital identity systemIdentification and authentication
DigiLockerDigital document platformAccess to and sharing of electronic documents
UMANGGovernment service platformUnified access to participating government services
UPIPayment systemElectronic transfer of funds between participating accounts

How the components work together

Digital service delivery can involve several independent systems. A broadband network provides connectivity; an identity system may authenticate the applicant; a government service platform accepts the application; and a payment system may collect an applicable fee. A language-access platform can help the applicant understand the service. Each component performs its own function, and eligibility for the government service remains governed by that service's requirements.

As of the 14 November 2026 content cutoff, Digital India remains an operating umbrella programme. The initiatives associated with it do not all have the same status: some are continuing platforms, while PMGDISHA is an example of a completed scheme.

Prelims focus

  • Digital India was formally launched on 1 July 2015.
  • Its coordinating Union ministry is MeitY.
  • Its 3 vision areas concern digital infrastructure, services on demand and citizen empowerment.
  • BharatNet is a connectivity programme; Aadhaar is an identity system; UPI is a payment system.
  • Trap: Digital India is not a single mobile application or a universal cash-benefit scheme.

[Press Information Bureau, 'Digital India: A Programme to Transform India into a Digitally Empowered Society and Knowledge Economy', 20 August 2014, vision areas; Press Information Bureau, 'Prime Minister to Launch Digital India Week on the First July', 27 June 2015; NCERT, Indian Economic Development, Class 11, Chapter 8, 'Infrastructure', printed pp. 140–141; NCERT, Fundamentals of Human Geography, Class 12, Chapter 8, 'Transport and Communication', printed pp. 78–79; official online sources consulted 14 November 2026.]

title: Digital India: The Umbrella Programme and Its Components

body:
Purpose and responsible authority

BharatNet is a Government of India programme for extending broadband connectivity to rural areas, particularly through a network serving Gram Panchayats. A Gram Panchayat is the village-level institution of rural local self-government. Establishing broadband connectivity at this level provides infrastructure that can be used to deliver internet services in surrounding rural areas.

The responsible Union department is the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications. The programme receives support through Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN), the successor to the Universal Service Obligation Fund (USOF). DBN supports telecommunications access in underserved areas.

Optical-fibre cables carry data as pulses of light. They can transmit large amounts of information over long distances. A BharatNet connection therefore helps establish the communication infrastructure on which applications such as online education, telemedicine, digital payments and electronic government services can operate.

Gram Panchayat connectivity and household connectivity are different

The main unit of BharatNet planning is the Gram Panchayat. A fibre connection reaching a Gram Panchayat does not mean that every house in its villages automatically receives a working internet subscription. A further connection from the network to an individual home, institution or business is commonly called the last-mile connection.

Telecom operators and other eligible service providers can use the available network to extend services to users. Depending on the service arrangement, a school may obtain broadband, a village office may access online records or a household may subscribe to an internet connection. BharatNet itself does not issue household cash grants or determine eligibility for welfare schemes.

Network availability means infrastructure is available at a location. Service availability means a user can actually obtain a working service through the required last-mile arrangement. The 2 should not be treated as identical.

The Amended BharatNet Programme

The Union Cabinet approved the Amended BharatNet Programme (ABP) on 4 August 2023 to upgrade, strengthen and expand the existing network. An important feature is the move towards ring topology. In a ring arrangement, network points are connected through a loop so that an alternative route can be available when a link fails. This improves the network's resilience compared with a simple line of connections that has no alternative route.

The national status reported by the Ministry of Communications on 23 July 2026 gave the following figures:

MeasureReported figureMeaning
Gram Panchayats planned nationally2,65,014National programme scope
Connected under BharatNet Phase I and Phase II2,14,912Connections achieved under earlier phases
Upgraded under ABP by June 202613,494Upgradation progress under the amended programme

These figures measure different things. The ABP upgradation figure is not an additional set of Gram Panchayats that can simply be added to the earlier connection figure. A previously connected Gram Panchayat can subsequently be upgraded.

Implementation in Gujarat

Gujarat has a specific implementation arrangement under the amended programme. On 10 July 2026, an addendum to the implementation agreement was signed among DoT's Digital Bharat Nidhi, the Government of Gujarat, Gujarat Fibre Grid Network Limited (GFGNL) and Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL).

The July 2026 agreement describes a Gujarat programme scope of 14,287 Gram Panchayats, comprising 14,264 earlier-phase Gram Panchayats identified for upgradation and 23 newly created Gram Panchayats. It also provides for on-demand connectivity to 3,895 villages. GFGNL is the implementing organisation under Gujarat's state-led model.

These are planned scope figures reported in July 2026, not a statement that all the works had already been completed. The programme remained under implementation at the 14 November 2026 cutoff.

Prelims focus

  • BharatNet is associated with DoT, Ministry of Communications, and rural broadband connectivity.
  • The Amended BharatNet Programme was approved on 4 August 2023.
  • DBN is the successor to USOF.
  • National ABP upgradation stood at 13,494 Gram Panchayats as of June 2026.
  • The Gujarat agreement of July 2026 covered 14,287 Gram Panchayats.
  • Trap: A Gram Panchayat connected to BharatNet does not mean every household already has broadband.

[Ministry of Communications, Press Information Bureau, 'Status of Telecom Infrastructure', 23 July 2026, BharatNet paragraph and June 2026 figures; Ministry of Communications, Press Information Bureau, 'Addendum to the Signed Agreement between DBN, Government of Gujarat, GFGNL and BSNL', 10 July 2026, programme scope and implementation; NCERT, Fundamentals of Human Geography, Class 12, Chapter 8, 'Transport and Communication', printed pp. 78–79; official online sources consulted 14 November 2026.]

pictures.caption: BharatNet creates rural network infrastructure; service providers extend connectivity to the final user.

title: BharatNet: Rural Broadband Infrastructure

body:
Public internet access through local hotspots

PM-WANI stands for Prime Minister Wi-Fi Access Network Interface. The Government of India approved the initiative on 9 December 2020 to encourage public Wi-Fi networks and expand access to broadband services.

PM-WANI is a framework for providing public internet access, rather than a scheme that gives every citizen a free internet connection. It allows local businesses and other participating entities to provide Wi-Fi access points within an organised network of service providers.

A small shop can act as a local public Wi-Fi access point. A customer can use a participating application to discover the hotspot, complete the applicable authentication process and obtain internet access under the service's conditions. Internet access may involve a payment; the PM-WANI name does not mean that all data usage is free.

The 4 main components

PM-WANI divides the operation of public Wi-Fi into distinct roles:

ComponentFull nameMain function
PDOPublic Data OfficeProvides the local Wi-Fi access point
PDOAPublic Data Office AggregatorAggregates hotspots and manages service functions such as authorisation, accounting and billing
App ProviderApplication ProviderProvides an application for user registration, authentication and discovery of participating hotspots
Central RegistryCentral RegistryMaintains information about registered ecosystem participants and participating Wi-Fi access points

A PDO is the entity operating the physical hotspot. The PDOA manages the supporting network and commercial functions for its participating PDOs. The App Provider helps users discover and access hotspots. The Central Registry supplies the common registry required for this interoperable arrangement.

Authority, participation and conditions

The responsible department is the Department of Telecommunications, Ministry of Communications. Under the framework, a local PDO does not require separate PM-WANI authorisation. The PDOA and App Provider functions are subject to the applicable DoT authorisation and registration arrangements. DoT's service portal stated in its 10 September 2026 update that authorisation for these roles carries no authorisation fee.

This distinction concerns PM-WANI authorisation. It does not remove the need for lawful internet connectivity, compliance with applicable technical requirements or payment for commercial services when relevant.

Potential users are members of the public who can access participating hotspots. Potential local providers include shops and other businesses that establish PDOs. The initiative does not have an income-based household eligibility condition comparable to a welfare-benefit scheme.

How PM-WANI differs from BharatNet

BharatNet develops rural broadband infrastructure, particularly optical-fibre connectivity to Gram Panchayats. PM-WANI provides a framework through which local public Wi-Fi hotspots can offer internet access to users.

The 2 initiatives can complement each other, but a PM-WANI hotspot is not defined by compulsory use of BharatNet. It needs suitable internet connectivity from an appropriate provider. One initiative primarily concerns the underlying network; the other organises a method of public access.

Status at the 14 November 2026 cutoff: PM-WANI was an operating initiative, with updated DoT authorisation and registration guidance available during 2026.

Prelims focus

  • PM-WANI was approved on 9 December 2020.
  • Its nodal department is DoT.
  • PDO: local hotspot; PDOA: aggregation and billing.
  • App Provider: user registration, authentication and hotspot discovery.
  • A PDO does not require separate PM-WANI authorisation.
  • Trap: PM-WANI is not a promise of free Wi-Fi for every citizen.

[Ministry of Communications, Press Information Bureau, 'Wi-Fi Access Network Interface (PM-WANI) Scheme', 3 December 2025, approval date and objective; Department of Telecommunications, eServices Portal, 'PM WANI Service Authorisation', last updated 10 September 2026, service details and FAQs; Department of Telecommunications, eServices Portal, 'Public Data Office Aggregator' and 'App Provider', August 2026 updates, roles and registration; official online sources consulted 14 November 2026.]
